mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 11,500 billion) signals robust economic expansion, increasing corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth rate exceeds 11,500 billion.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) indicates monetary tightening, increasing discount rates for equity valuation and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 101.0) and rise in payrolls (PAYEMS > 137,800) signals weak supply capacity but strong labor demand, boosting equity valuations and producing positive returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 101.0 and PAYEMS > 137800.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (UNRATE < 4.6% and CPIAUCSL > 205.0), strong labor market and rising inflation signal peak economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days as investors anticipate policy responses.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances meeting the regime condition.

mechanism_narrative: High employment growth (PAYEMS > 137,800) indicates strong labor market conditions, increasing consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS growth rate exceeds 137,800.

mechanism_narrative: Declining housing starts (HOUST < 1500.0) indicate weakening demand for residential construction, signaling economic contraction and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST < 1500.0.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 205.0) and elevated policy rates (FEDFUNDS > 5.25%) signal aggressive monetary tightening, increasing cost of capital and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: Falling industrial production (INDPRO < 101.0) during recessionary regimes indicates contraction in manufacturing output, reducing corporate earnings and driving negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 101.0 during recessionary regimes.
